entries.title: 2 fatally shot in Hyde Park
entries.summary: <p>Two people were fatally shot Thursday afternoon in Hyde Park, according to Chicago police.</p><p>A 24-year-old man and 27-year-old woman were found inside a vehicle in the 5900 block of East Ellis Avenue at 5:35 p.m. with single gunshot wounds to each of their heads, police said. They were both taken to University of Chicago Medical Center where they later died.</p><p>A dark sedan crashed on the east curb of Ellis Avenue with damage to its front, its airbags deployed and both front doors open. About a dozen officers processed the scene and put up red tape around 7 p.m.</p><p>No one was in custody.<br></p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Man killed, 13-year-old boy shot in West Garfield Park
entries.summary: <p>A man was killed and a boy hospitalized by a shooting in West Garfield Park Thursday night, according to Chicago police.</p><p>Two men fired shots at 6:50 p.m. in the 3800 block of West Adams Street, hitting a 49-year-old man on the sidewalk and a 13-year-old boy in a car, police said. The man was taken to Mt. Sinai Hospital where he later died.</p><p>The boy was taken to Stroger Hospital where he was listed in good condition, police said.</p><p>No one is in custody.<br></p>

entries.title: Pullman to celebrate century anniversary of Metra Electric line
entries.summary: <p>Historic railcars and interactive exhibits will be showcased this week in Pullman on the city's South Side to help celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Metra Electric line.</p><p>Officials made the announcement Thursday at a news conference at the Millennium Station Downtown.</p><p>The Railroad Days celebration, 10 a.m.- 4 p.m. Saturday and Sunday at Pullman Historical National Park, will feature a restored 1926 Pullman electric railcar and a vintage 1970s-era railcar. Visitors also can explore model train displays; a science, technology, engineering, art and math fair with hands-on science and engineering activities; food trucks; live music and presentations. Tickets are $20 before Saturday and $25 on Saturday and Sunday.</p><p>Friends of Pullman Executive Director Peggy Parfenoff said the transition from steam-powered locomotives to electric rail service helped transform the city.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-2d0000"
